why: The defect lives in real producer/consumer timing against real DB file sizes, and the unit test fakes both. DumperTest has 24,516 objects, which is 3 chunks of 8,192. With Game objects only, every captured object sits in chunk 3 (indices 19,510-24,515, per L66). The consumer polls only after non-empty chunks, so its first size/disk poll comes after the LAST chunk. If the DB is already over Max size, the stop therefore always fires after fetchedAll: deterministic. L66 measured the status half of this red on 025dc031^ (`first 24,516 of 24,516`). The persisted 'cap' that build 3549 adds was only code-read.

why: The fix is a flag predicate for a state that only a running 5.0-5.3 engine produces. Under the default gc.PendingKillEnabled=True (UE_5.1 BaseEngine.ini:1302; DumperTest51's Config does not override it), MarkAsGarbage takes MarkPendingKillOnlyInternal, which sets RF_PendingKill 0x20000000 and item bit 29, and neither Garbage bit (UE_5.1 UObjectBaseUtility.h:60-64,264-275). The unit test only feeds synthetic flags. DumperTest51 is a stock 5.1.1 build: detected version 501, classic item layout (24 bytes Shipping, 32 bytes Development), sparse storage located (SPARSE_ES2_1). It has no WeakToGarbage lever, and AController::StartSpot is not a UPROPERTY in 5.1. The pawn's capsule does carry two engine-made sparse bindings to CharMoveComp: OnComponentBeginOverlap->CapsuleTouched and PhysicsVolumeChangedDelegate->PhysicsVolumeChanged, both added in SetUpdatedComponent. Neither is removed when the actor is destroyed, and FSparseDelegateStorage drops an entry only when GC deletes the object.
